claim: Derived: the Amdahl ceiling for regulatory review inside total development time. A standard PDUFA action period of 10 months (priority 6 months) plus the 60-day filing period is roughly 10-12 months out of a total development span commonly cited at 10-15 years, i.e. about 5.5-10% of elapsed time. Even eliminating FDA review entirely - which the CNPV pilot approximates at 1-2 months - would shorten total elapsed development by only about 5-8%.
source_title: Derived Amdahl ceiling for FDA review share of development time

figures.metric: FDA review share of total development elapsed time
figures.denominator_def: 10-12 months review divided by 120-180 months total development

derivation: Low: 10/180 = 5.6%. High: 12/120 = 10.0%. Midpoint ~7.5%. The 10-15 year total development span is an ANCHOR UNDER TEST per the common brief and is not treated here as verified; the derived share is therefore a bounded estimate, not a settled figure. Inputs: E-4033, E-4053.

claim: Derived: regional in-house review staffing per novel approval. CDER+CBER at 6,383 staff produced 46 novel CDER approvals in 2025 (139 staff per novel approval); EMA at about 897 staff produced 38 new active substances (24 staff per new active substance) but leans on over 4,500 external national-agency experts; PMDA at about 873 staff with 560 technical reviewers. These ratios show that agency in-house headcount is not a simple predictor of approval output because the EU externalises assessment.
source_title: Derived staffing-per-approval ratios across FDA, EMA, PMDA

figures.metric: CDER+CBER staff per novel CDER approval 2025
figures.denominator_def: 6,383 CDER+CBER staff divided by 46 novel CDER approvals in 2025

derivation: 6383/46 = 138.8. 897/38 = 23.6. Caveat: FDA staff also handle generics, OTC, supplements, inspections and post-market work not counted in the denominator, and EMA outsources assessment to national agencies, so cross-region comparison of these ratios is indicative only.
